decision: The offboarding process is approved once conductor.b folds in the panel's conditions. Open question answered: yes, the conductor may archive a session after its own hand-over without asking each time, for routine hand-overs (case 1) only; retiring a site agent (case 2) or a role (case 3), and fast stops, still go to Dinis.
conditions: Archive without asking only when: the hand-over note is committed and linked; the successor has confirmed in writing that it works; nothing still fires into the old session (step 4 actually done, not open); steps 3 to 7 are shown done by cited commits or quoted UTC times, not by the leaving agent's word; the archive line is recorded (step 9).

Vault keys: before archiving, every vault key the leaving agent held or could open has a live holder other than the leaving key, always including the account's maestro, sealed to the current maestro key. When a maestro is offboarded, every copy sealed to its session key is re-sealed to the successor first: re-seal, check, then archive, from a named list.

Keys: step 3 retires the key in the agent's own repository too (keys now live there), and says whether it counts as done on dev or on merge. Backup copies of a retired key are destroyed, not re-sealed.

Step 1 also lists the agent's inbox lanes, its area page, its scheduled wakes (by id) and any personal or third-party data the transcript holds; step 9 repoints or closes lanes and the area page. Secrets are named in the transcript, never printed; the record says the transcript survives an archive.
Repointing an agent's own wakes to a successor of the same role is a standing yes; only creating new tasks needs Dinis.

Step 8 says who archives a maestro and who archives a conductor; 'after Dinis has seen the hand-over' becomes a cited UTC time and quote, or falls away for case 1. Step 7's 'his word, never a record' is rewritten plainly.
Site owners are told when their site's agent changes or retires: who the new agent is, where its key is, and that nothing they own has moved.
Each archived session is counted in status.json so the saving shows. For routine hand-overs it is a one-screen checklist in the hand-over note. Step 1's duplicate 'sessions it created' is removed.
note: A choice, not a push. The revised draft's push is factory.b's or conductor.b's under the usual checks.
